newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends flat vs dlr, demand seen low.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends flat vs dlr, demand seen low.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed little changed against the dollar on Tuesday as a lack of demand kept the U.S. currency from gaining on the rupee, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.49 after opening around the same level.
The dollar rose to 57.60 in the morning, mostly on speculation, before slipping again, dealers said.
"Overseas, the dollar has been down during the past few days and at home, there hasn't been much genuine demand," a Hatton National Bank dealer said.
The central bank pushed the dollar and fixed buying and selling prices at 56.8805 and 58.0296.
"The market was not totally flat," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer. "There are sellers and there are buyers. The market can absorb dollars either way."
Overnight call money closed at 12.75 with the market highly liquid, dealers said.
